subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and shared/private memory boundaries should become the public contract?
rationale: The request creates durable agents, workspaces, skills, config, memory, and routing authority from group-chat senders, which cannot be inferred safely from existing DM dynamic agents or thread-bound subagent bindings.

options.title: Design Generic Contract First
options.body: Define admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle, private/shared memory tiers, quotas, and cleanup as reusable channel/plugin contracts before adding Feishu behavior.

options.title: Keep Current Supported Paths
options.body: Document groupSessionScope, static bindings, and explicit thread-bound subagents as the supported Feishu group-chat model for now.

options.title: Route To External Plugin
options.body: Reject automatic provisioning in core and let a Feishu-specific external plugin own durable group identity policy if current plugin seams are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Contract First
recommendation.body: Define admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle, private/shared memory tiers, quotas, and cleanup as reusable channel/plugin contracts before adding Feishu behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They show the broadest recent history across Feishu docs/runtime and are the best available routing owner for the product-boundary decision.
